Cloudora 1.0.6 lets a drive be shared. One person keeps the channel, and the
rest of the family or the team signs in with their own Telegram account and
sees the same files. There is still no Cloudora server and no new account:
the files stay in the channel on Telegram.

More about it, and step-by-step install guides, at https://protechph.github.io/Cloudora/

## What's new

- **Share the drive.** In Settings · Drive channel · Invite people, send the
  channel's link. The other person joins it in Telegram, opens Cloudora, and
  the drive is there. Their phone finds it on its own.
- **You decide what each person can do.** Cloudora follows Telegram's own
  admin rights. An **editor** can add files, rename, move, star, trash, make
  albums and back up photos. A **viewer** can browse, watch, listen, download
  and keep files offline, and that is all. Make someone an admin with Post,
  edit and delete in Telegram to make them an editor.
- **Switch drive.** Settings · Drive channel · Switch drive opens another
  drive this account can use, with the role it has there. The phone forgets
  what it kept for the old drive first, and says so before it does.
- **Private stays the owner's.** A shared drive's Private folders open for the
  owner alone. Cloudora says plainly that this hides them in Cloudora only,
  while Telegram still shows their files to everyone in the channel.
- **A drive that is gone says so.** Removed from the channel, or the channel
  deleted, the app now says the shared drive isn't available anymore instead
  of quietly making a new, empty one.
- **Read-only really is read-only.** A viewer's phone offers no action that
  would be refused. It also writes nothing in the background: no index copy,
  no trash purge, no previews, no backup.
- **One photo timeline for everyone.** Photo backup from every phone lands in
  the same drive, and a photo already there is not sent again.

## Which file to download

- **Android, most phones:** `cloudora-1.0.6-arm64-v8a.apk`
- **Android, older phones:** `cloudora-1.0.6-armeabi-v7a.apk`
- **Chromebooks and emulators:** `cloudora-1.0.6-x86_64.apk`
- **iPhone:** `cloudora-1.0.6.ipa`, installed with Sideloadly, SideStore or AltStore and your own Apple Account. Follow the [iPhone guide](https://protechph.github.io/Cloudora/iphone.html); it shows every step.

`cloudora-1.0.6.aab` is the same Android app as a bundle for app stores; you
don't need it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.

## Good to know

- **The choice is per phone.** Signing in on a new phone opens the account's
  own drive again if it has one; the shared drive is one Switch drive away.
- **The owner's account is the channel's.** If it goes, the drive goes with it.
- **Being invited while already using Cloudora** changes nothing on screen
  until Settings · Drive channel is opened. The invite is the instruction.

## On iPhone

The iPhone app opens the same drive, shared drives included. Photo backup
runs while the app is open, and the Google Photos import, watched folders,
the document scanner and sharing in from other apps aren't on iPhone yet.
Apps installed this way need a refresh once a week; the guide shows how.

## Support

Cloudora is free, with no ads. If it's useful to you, you can [send a tip on
Jami](https://jami.bio/jericko). If something doesn't work, [report a
problem](https://github.com/protechph/Cloudora/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml).
